COLLECTIVE AGREEMENT
OF
Messrs. Shriro Bros. (China), Fod. Inc. U. S. A.

1. The management agrees to grant same wages, allowance and rice allowance as those paid in the Worsted Department of the Ewo Cotton Mill.

2. The female workers who have been worked over one year shall be granted one month's leave with full wages, allowance and rice allowance during the period of child-birth.

3. In the event of a worker sustaining injury in performance of his duty, he shall be sent to the hospital designated by the management. Besides medical and hospital expenses, full wages, allowance and rice allowance will be paid by the management during the period of hospital treatment.

4. The management grants the following seven days as holidays with full wages, allowance and rice allowance:-
(1) Establishment of the Republic of China - (January 1st) one day
(2) Lunar New Year - two days
(3) Dragon Boat Festival - One day
(4) Labor Day - (May 1st) one day
(5) Mid-Autumn Festival - one day
(6) National Holiday (October 10th) - one day

Workers employed on any above mentioned holidays will be paid double wages, allowance and rice allowance.

5. The management shall not dismiss any worker without just cause. Those who violate the Rules and Regulations of the Factory will be dismissed.

6. The management agrees to pay a discharging allowance to the twelve dismissed workers according to the months of their service upon the following basis:-

Three days pay including allowance and rice allowance to those who were employed one month. A minimum will be paid of fifteen days' pay including allowance and rice allowance to those who were employed less than five months.

7. The workers shall not in future declare a strike. Any reasonable demands shall be presented to the management by their representatives for direct negotiations. Either party may request the Shanghai Municipal Council for mediation, if direct negotiation are without success.

respectively, and five workers' representatives took place
in the Division Office at 10 a.m. July 15th and 17th. Mr.
Saxl stated that the management has granted two increases
in wages and allowance this year and are paying same wages
and allowances as these of the Kwo Worsted Mill, these
companies being competitors in the same trade, and so the
management would not consider any further increase in wages
or allowance at present. Furthermore, the Company is short
of raw material for normal operation in spite of efforts made
to secure these abroad. Thus the management would be glad
to suspend operations for two months, in case the workers
wish to have a longer strike. The workers stated that their
present earnings could not meet the present cost of living
and insisted their demands be met before they would resume
work. Efforts have been made to persuade the former to
grant some concessions in treatment and the later to reduce
their demands to a minimum.

Further negotiations between the representatives of
the both parties proceeded at the same office at 2:30 p.m.
July 21st and 23rd. The management agreed to consider the
demands for maternity benefit, medical expenses and wages
for injury in performance of duty, wages for holidays and
overtime pay, but refused to consider any increase in wages
or allowance. They agreed also to consider that at the time
of slackness, surplus number of workers be paid a discharging
allowance of one day's pay for every month's service. The
workers' representatives insisted either an increase in wages
or allowances be granted besides the other demands. Both
parties were still very firm in their attitudes, and therefore
a deadlock was reached. They were informed by the Industrial
Relations Officer that mediation would be temporarily suspended
as long as their attitudes remained firm, but willing to take
up further mediation in the future if they would reconsider
their attitudes.

分别于7月15日和17日上午10时在该处办公室与五名工人代表进行了谈判。Saxl 先生表示，资方今年已两次增加工资和津贴，目前支付的工资和津贴与国毛纺织厂（Kwo Worsted Mill）相同，这两家公司是同行业的竞争对手，因此资方目前不考虑进一步增加工资或津贴。此外，尽管努力从国外获取原材料，但公司仍缺乏正常运营所需的原料。因此，如果工人希望延长罢工时间，资方乐意暂停运营两个月。工人表示，他们目前的收入无法应付当前的生活成本，并坚持在满足其要求之前不会复工。已努力劝说前者在待遇上做出一些让步，并劝说后者将其要求降至最低限度。

双方代表于7月21日和23日下午2时30分在同一办公室进行了进一步谈判。资方同意考虑产假福利、工伤医疗费用及工资、节假日工资和加班费的要求，但拒绝考虑任何增加工资或津贴的要求。他们还同意考虑在生意清淡时，向多余的人员支付遣散费，标准为每服务一个月支付一天的工资。工人代表坚持除了其他要求外，还必须增加工资或津贴。双方态度依然非常强硬，因此陷入僵局。劳资关系官员告知他们，只要他们的态度保持强硬，调解将暂时中止，但如果他们重新考虑其态度，愿意在未来进行进一步调解。

D.S. Edgar.

Sir,
At 6.50 a.m., even date a telephone message was
received at this Station from the above factory to the
effect that the strikers were causing trouble on Baikal
Road.

In response to this message a party of Police atten-
ded and later brought to the Station one Zang Wen Liang
(张文良) representative of Social Movement Guide Com-
mittee (社会运动指导委员会) for further enquiries.

Enquiries made by detectives ascertained that since
the 14-2-41, the above factory has been operating daily
with a depleted staff- consisting of non-union members.
Meantime, the Management had also engaged appro-
ximately 20 new employees in the Western District, how-
ever, when these employees were on their way to the
factory this morning to commence work, the motor-van
was intercepted on Baikal Road by the strikers and
forced to stop.

A discussion of short duration between the two
factions took place and culminated in the newly engaged
employees returning home, the entire party refusing to
proceed to the factory. When the latter people departed
the strikers soon dispersed and only a few remained when
the Police arrived on the scene.

Zang Wen Liang in accounting for his presence on
Baikal Road explained that he went there purposely to
mediate with the factory Management on behalf of the
strikers.

Employees demands learned to be:-
(1) Increased pay- amount not specified.

侦探长 Edgar。

先生，
当日早上6时50分，本捕房接到上述工厂的电话留言，称罢工者在贝加尔路（Baikal Road）制造麻烦。

作为对该留言的回应，一队警察前往现场，随后将一名社会运动指导委员会（Social Movement Guide Committee）的代表张文良（Zang Wen Liang）带回捕房作进一步查询。

经侦探查询查明，自1941年2月14日起，上述工厂每日由非工会成员组成的精简人员维持运营。同时，管理层也在西区雇佣了约20名新员工，然而，当这些员工今天早上前往工厂开始工作时，他们的货车在贝加尔路被罢工者拦截并被迫停下。

两派之间进行了短暂的讨论，最终导致新雇佣的员工回家，全体人员拒绝前往工厂。当后者离开时，罢工者很快散去，警察到达现场时仅剩少数几人。

张文良解释他在贝加尔路出现的原因时称，他是特意去那里代表罢工者与工厂管理层进行调解的。

获悉的雇员要求如下：
(1) 加薪——金额未指定。

Sir,
At 5.30 p.m., 12-2-41, a telephone message was
received from the management of the above concern,
located at No. 694 Wetmore Road, reporting that the
employees had struck work and had left the factory.
Enquiries made by C.D.C. 262, C.D.S. 235 and the
undersigned ascertained that a popular movement was
underway by the employees of the above factory (appro-
ximately 185) where only non-union members are employed,
to become members of the Social Movement Guide Committee
(社會運動指導委員會) (A Nanking regime sponsored institu-
tion) with branch office at 1963/12 Yangtsepoo Road.
Head office 527 Range Road.
At p.m. even date the management of the factory
learned of the movement, and forthwith notified the
employees that the services of anyone joining the afore-
mentioned institution would be dispensed with immediate-
ly. The workers when confronted with their alternative
struck work (en bloc) and left the factory, presumably
to discuss the matter more thoroughly outside.
The above factory normally closes down at 5.30
p.m. daily.
No untoward incident occurred.

I am, Sir,
Your Obedient Servant,

My name is Ss Ngoh-ding, age 31, a native of Ningpo, residing at No.7 Sing Vee Shing Li (新惟兴里), Pingliang Road near Thorburn Road. I have been in the employ of the Dyeing Department of the Shriro Brothers, an American owned cotton weaving factory, 496 Wetmore Road as worker No.411, since March, 1940.

In 1935 I was employed by the An Tai (安泰) Iron Factory, corner of Kwenming and Dalny Roads, where I worked for over two years. In 1938 I found employment at the Dyeing Department of the New Ewo Cotton Mill, Yangtsepoo Road, and stayed there about half a year.

On July 4, in consequence of a decision by the management of the factory to prolong the working hours by one or two hours each day between Monday and Friday every week, instead of operating six days a week, I and three other workers, named Chow Chung (周鈞), Koo Tse-sung (顧志仁) and Ting Yee-yuen (丁以元) were elected as representatives and requested the management to issue us with rice allowance for Saturdays, although no work was done on that day. We were later dismissed by the management for agitation. On learning of our dismissal, the other fellow-workers, 23 in number, of the same department, walked out during the afternoon of the same day.

On the afternoon of July 7, we, the four representatives proceeded to the Industrial Section of the S.M.C. and presented an appeal for assistance and mediation in the dispute. A member of the Industrial Section made a telephone call to
